doc.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Turning down gigs and playing Dixieland
summary: He turned down gigs that carried hassle or poor pay, on principle; Dixieland gigs are still great.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I’m wondering if you — go ahead — if you ever turned, at that time, you’re in New York trying to make a living, I imagine that the typical jazz gig, which you were happy to get, probably didn’t pay that much? So did you ever turn down a gig at that time?
For not being it paid well enough?
Yes. Usually the gig wasn’t worth it anyway.
What kind of gig might it have been?

Where there was any kind of hustle or hassle, you know I mean it had to be credible. I mean people who were paying enough money had the better gigs than the ones who didn’t you know. I mean it was a matter of not so much the money but just principles.
Were you ever asked to do the Dixieland thing?
Yeah, that was great. It’s still great.
As a tuba player you’re the bass player.
